user.title: Which player?
user.description: DriveLyrics shows synced lyrics for what this media player plays — on your car's screen, a phone or any browser.

data_description.player: For a Tesla: the car's media player from the Tesla Fleet, Teslemetry or Tessie integration.
data_description.server: Only change this if you run DriveLyrics yourself.

enable_player.title: Turn on your car's media player?
enable_player.description: Your car's media player is turned off in Home Assistant (Tesla Fleet ships it that way). DriveLyrics needs it to know what's playing. Turn it on now?

reauth_confirm.title: Link DriveLyrics again
reauth_confirm.description: DriveLyrics no longer accepts this link (it was removed in DriveLyrics' settings). Link again to keep showing lyrics.

abort.already_configured: This player is already linked to DriveLyrics.
abort.cannot_connect: Could not reach DriveLyrics. Check the internet connection and try again.
abort.link_denied: The link was denied in DriveLyrics. Nothing was linked.
abort.link_expired: The link expired before it was approved. Start again.
abort.player_gone: That media player no longer exists.

progress.wait_for_approval: Open [DriveLyrics]({url}), sign in if asked, check that it shows the code **{code}** and tap **Approve**. This finishes by itself once approved; the code is valid for 10 minutes.

data.refresh: Refresh the player before each answer
data.push_on_change: Send track changes as soon as the player reports them

data_description.refresh: Needed for a car: its integration only reads the car when asked (for a Tesla, one billed vehicle data request per answer). Turn off for players that update on their own.
data_description.push_on_change: While a DriveLyrics screen is open. Costs nothing extra: nothing is read, what the player already reported is sent.
data_description.reads_per_hour: Up to 20 of them at once (skipping tracks, tapping refresh), then spread over the hour. A screen open while music plays needs about 15–20 an hour. Tesla bills $0.002 per vehicle data read (Fleet API, 500 per $1) and gives a $10 monthly credit (5,000 reads). These limits are this Home Assistant's own safety lock, on top of the budget in DriveLyrics' settings (default 800 a month): whatever DriveLyrics asks, Home Assistant reads the car no more than this. When a limit is reached, DriveLyrics gets what Home Assistant already knows instead, and says so on screen.
data_description.monthly_reads: Counted per calendar month (UTC). The default 3,000 (about $6) stays within Tesla's credit and leaves 2,000 reads for Home Assistant's own use of the car's API. Tesla bills $0.002 per vehicle data read (Fleet API, 500 per $1) and gives a $10 monthly credit (5,000 reads). These limits are this Home Assistant's own safety lock, on top of the budget in DriveLyrics' settings (default 800 a month): whatever DriveLyrics asks, Home Assistant reads the car no more than this. When a limit is reached, DriveLyrics gets what Home Assistant already knows instead, and says so on screen.

auth_failed.message: DriveLyrics no longer accepts this link.

feed_not_selected.title: DriveLyrics isn't showing what Home Assistant sends
feed_not_selected.description: Home Assistant is linked, but your DriveLyrics screens show Spotify instead. In DriveLyrics, open Settings → Now-playing feed and choose the feed under "Now playing from".

read_limit_hourly.title: DriveLyrics reached its hourly limit for reading {name}
read_limit_hourly.description: DriveLyrics asked for more than {limit} car reads an hour (the limit you set in this integration's options). Until the limit allows a read again, Home Assistant answers with what it already knows without reading the car, so a track change can show late; the DriveLyrics screen says so. Nothing is broken. If this happens often, raise **Car reads per hour** in the integration's options (Settings → Devices & services → DriveLyrics → Configure). You are told this once; the **Read limit** sensor always shows the current state.

read_limit_monthly.title: DriveLyrics reached this month's limit for reading {name}
read_limit_monthly.description: This month Home Assistant has read the car {limit} times for DriveLyrics, the limit you set in this integration's options. Until the month ends (UTC), DriveLyrics gets what Home Assistant already knows without reading the car, so track changes can show late; the DriveLyrics screen says so. To allow more, raise **Car reads per month** in the integration's options (Settings → Devices & services → DriveLyrics → Configure).
